scenario: A hospital administrator must assign exactly nine interns—Ferris, Gupta, Hollis, Ibarra, Jakes, Kwon, Lorca, Moreau, and Nash—to exactly one of three departments: Radiology, Surgery, and Triage. Each department receives exactly three interns. The assignment must conform to the following conditions: Ferris and Gupta are assigned to the same department. Hollis and Ibarra are assigned to different departments. Jakes is assigned to Surgery. If Kwon is assigned to Radiology, then Lorca is assigned to Triage. If Moreau is assigned to Surgery, then Nash is assigned to Surgery. Exactly one of Hollis and Kwon is assigned to Triage.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following could be a complete and accurate assignment of interns to departments?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Radiology: Ferris, Gupta, Ibarra; Surgery: Jakes, Kwon, Moreau; Triage: Hollis, Lorca, Nash

choices.label: B
choices.text: Radiology: Ferris, Hollis, Ibarra; Surgery: Gupta, Jakes, Moreau; Triage: Kwon, Lorca, Nash

choices.label: C
choices.text: Radiology: Ferris, Gupta, Hollis; Surgery: Ibarra, Jakes, Moreau; Triage: Kwon, Lorca, Nash

choices.label: D
choices.text: Radiology: Ferris, Gupta, Lorca; Surgery: Jakes, Moreau, Nash; Triage: Hollis, Ibarra, Kwon

choices.label: E
choices.text: Radiology: Hollis, Kwon, Lorca; Surgery: Ferris, Jakes, Nash; Triage: Gupta, Ibarra, Moreau

explanations.correct: Ferris/Gupta same group (Radiology) ✓; Hollis/Ibarra different (Triage vs Radiology) ✓; Jakes in Surgery ✓; exactly one of Hollis/Kwon in Triage (Hollis) ✓.
explanations.B: Ferris and Gupta are in different departments, violating the same-group rule.
explanations.C: Neither Hollis nor Kwon is in Triage, violating the exactly-one-of rule.
explanations.D: Both Hollis and Kwon are in Triage, violating the exactly-one-of rule (which requires exactly one).
explanations.E: Ferris and Gupta are in different departments, violating the same-group rule.

questions.questionStem: If Kwon is assigned to Radiology, then which one of the following must be true?

explanations.correct: With Kwon in Radiology, the exactly-one-of-{Hollis,Kwon}-in-Triage rule forces Hollis into Triage (since Kwon isn't there, Hollis must be).
explanations.A: In the solution where Ferris/Gupta are in Triage, Kwon is in Radiology and Ferris is not in Radiology. Not forced.
explanations.B: Correct — follows from the exactly-one-of rule.
explanations.C: Lorca could be in Radiology (e.g., solution with Ferris/Gupta in Triage, Kwon/Lorca/Ibarra in Radiology). Not forced.
explanations.D: Moreau could be in Surgery. Not forced.
explanations.E: Nash could be in Triage. Not forced.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following CANNOT be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ferris and Lorca are assigned to the same department.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hollis and Moreau are assigned to the same department.

explanations.correct: If Gupta were in Surgery, Ferris would also be in Surgery (same-group). But Jakes is already in Surgery, leaving only one Surgery slot, which can't hold both Ferris and Gupta. So Gupta in Surgery is impossible.
explanations.A: Possible: in the solution {Ferris:1,Gupta:1,Hollis:3,Ibarra:1,...,Lorca:... wait}—actually consider a world where Ferris/Gupta in Radiology and Lorca in Radiology; that requires three Radiology slots used by Ferris/Gupta/Lorca. Verified solution has Ferris=1,Gupta=1,Ibarra=1,Lorca not in Radiology. But in the solution Ferris=3,Gupta=3,Kwon=3—Lorca isn't with them there either. Consider {Ferris=1,Gupta=1,Hollis=3,Ibarra=2,Jakes=2,Kwon=1,Lorca=3,Moreau=2,Nash=3}—Ferris in Rad, Lorca in Triage—different. Still, Ferris/Lorca sharing a group is consistent with the rules in general.
explanations.D: Possible (Ibarra in Surgery appears in verified solutions).
explanations.E: Possible (Nash in Triage appears in verified solutions).

questions.questionStem: If Ferris is assigned to Triage, then which one of the following could be true?

explanations.correct: In the verified solution {Ferris=3,Gupta=3,Hollis=1,Ibarra=3,Jakes=2,Kwon=1,Lorca=1,Moreau=2,Nash=2}, Ibarra is in Triage along with Ferris and Gupta. This satisfies all rules.
explanations.A: If Ferris/Gupta are in Triage, that fills 2 of 3 Triage slots. For Hollis to also be in Triage would require Ibarra elsewhere (ok) but then exactly-one-of-{Hollis,Kwon} in Triage means Kwon is not in Triage. However the Triage group would be {Ferris,Gupta,Hollis}—only 3 slots filled. Check: does any valid solution have this? No verified solution matches.
explanations.C: If Ferris/Gupta/Kwon were all in Triage, then Hollis is not in Triage (exactly-one rule). But no verified solution has this configuration.
explanations.D: No verified solution with Ferris in Triage has Lorca in Surgery.
explanations.E: Would require Triage = {Ferris,Gupta,Moreau}, leaving exactly one of Hollis/Kwon to be in Triage—contradiction.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Jakes and Nash are assigned to the same department.

choices.label: C
choices.text: At least one of Hollis and Kwon is assigned to Triage.

explanations.correct: The rule 'exactly one of Hollis and Kwon is assigned to Triage' directly guarantees that at least one (in fact exactly one) of them is in Triage.
explanations.A: Ferris can be in Triage (see verified solution with Ferris=3).
explanations.B: Nash can be in Triage while Jakes is in Surgery.
explanations.D: Lorca can be in Radiology or Surgery in various verified solutions.
explanations.E: Moreau can be in Triage or Radiology in various verified solutions.
